<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-rule-schema-formats.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`  _(via object_extension (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES), object_extension (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via object_extension (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via object_extension (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via object_extension (literal, a string literal in runtimeTypes))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-rule-schema-formats.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `17df209a0b03adf7d71ad6a35e2e3959e7a55eb8` — the merge of head `d190a7f0437f6d0d40f1a2357023b12ce5b04993` into base `b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 17df209a0b03adf7d71ad6a35e2e3959e7a55eb8 && git checkout 17df209a0b03adf7d71ad6a35e2e3959e7a55eb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5 d190a7f0437f6d0d40f1a2357023b12ce5b04993 && git checkout -B drift-repro b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5 && git merge --no-ff d190a7f0437f6d0d40f1a2357023b12ce5b04993

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b63c894934b5e427b456b997774f48a220edb7e5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d190a7f0437f6d0d40f1a2357023b12ce5b04993`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-added-lookup-hop-leaf-judged.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-validation-rule-artifacts-judged.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rule-compilability.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rule-schema-formats.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts

PR #33398, cards #33216 and #33217 (two commits, `1ab94153` and `d190a7f0`). Inputs: both cards with every comment (through 6882304973 on #33216 and 6881180427 on #33217), the PR body and file list (12 files), the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` (`objectExtensionsByTarget`, `objectsAsServed`, `objectsWithoutTiedFields`), `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` (snapshot set, differential, `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor`), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`mergeValidationsByName`), `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`ObjectExtensionSchema.validations`) and `field-value.zod.ts` (`referenceCarrierOf`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, build (`os build` / `os validate` / `os lint`), #33216: right.** `refuseUndeclaredHopField` and the hop refusal's `storedMetadataBodyReferencesFor(objectName, true)` now read the hopping reference off `typedObjects` (the served fold, tied fields dropped). Newly refused: `record.REF.LEAF` in a validation rule or a formula where `REF` is a lookup an `objectExtensions` entry adds and the target serves no `LEAF`, wherever the expression is written (the extension's rule or field, or the object's own rule or formula). A stack with no extension is untouched: `objectsAsServed` returns the declared array itself, so `typedObjects` is `objects`.
- **Accept-set, build, #33217: right.** `walkObjectValidationRules` appends each rule of each entry `objectExtensionsByTarget` keeps, so the three existing rule ids now fire on an extension's `format` / `json_schema` rule. The walk has two callers only (`validateRuleCompilability`, `validateRuleSchemaFormats`); no third reader inherits the wider set.
- **Accept-set, `object_extension` door: right.** `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('object_extension')` now returns four rules (`validateStackExpressions`, `validateSecurityRoleWord`, `validateRuleCompilability`, `validateRuleSchemaFormats`). `objectExtensions` is not a context key, so the baseline carries none and the candidate carries the written entry alone: the target's own rules in `objects` fingerprint identically in both passes and cancel, and the entry's findings (`objectExtensions[0]...`) cannot cancel.
- **Accept-set, `object` door and every other door: unchanged, right.** Those snapshots carry no `objectExtensions`, so neither the served reading nor the new loop sees anything.
- **Public surface: right.** No exported signature or type shape moves. `walkObjectValidationRules` (exported from the lint index) returns more rows and `WalkedValidationRule`'s jsdoc says so; no schema, no spec key, no generated baseline.
- **Gates.** Check-runs on the head at review time (65 listed): 24 success (among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate), 10 skipped (opt-in or not applicable), 31 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint and Repo Gates), 0 failed. This record reads no verdict off the 31 pending runs; they stay the queue's to hold, and a red one is not covered here.

### ② Semver level

Right. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value an author could publish is now refused) takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves: `@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor (the two new semantic entries), both in the one changeset. `@objectstack/runtime` moves only a test file. The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner with Before / Now / Unchanged / Fix, and one `adr-0087: registered` marker naming both entry ids, which match the `id` fields in the two files. Check Changeset concluded success on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — present, identically armed, on the PR body and the changeset; it agrees with the diff (no exported type or signature change, two refusals added).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report (6882304973).
- Out-of-scope note, "a field an extension redeclares on the target with a different reference is now read as served at a hop site": answered, correct as built. The engine plans the hop over the registered schema, and the object walk's #24677 field verdict deliberately keeps the declared body; no card owed.
- Deviations: the three file-surface amendments are each recorded on the cards before the push (6881000954, 6881018477, 6881180427) and match the file list; the changeset and docs edit riding the second commit is harmless on a squash.
- Fences held: the diff does not touch `buildNullableFieldIndex` or the `extensionWrite` strip (#33246's), and folds neither #33153 nor #33101.
- No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.object-extension-added-lookup-hop-leaf-judged.ts` (#33216): holds.** Read sentence by sentence against `validate-expressions.ts` at the head. Surface: both sites that serve a hop (`check` with `traversalHydration`, `judgeFieldFormula`) call the two refusals with the target's name, in the object walk and in the extension walk, so "a validation rule or a formula" is exact, and the example (lookup and formula in one entry) folds into the same served body. Replacement: the leaf is judged against `fieldIndex`, built over `servedObjects` with the injected columns, plus `id`: "its own fields, the columns the platform injects, every field an extension adds, or `id`" is what the code accepts. Reason: same message builder (`undeclaredHopFieldMessage`), same rule id, located by the caller's `where`; the stored-metadata-body sentence is the `served` flag; the tie sentence is `objectsWithoutTiedFields`. Tried to break it: a declared lookup keeps its own definition in the fold, so no declared verdict moves; a target outside the stack or the door closure has no index and stays unjudged; an undeclared extension target matches no served object and is not judged; the #24677 field-reference verdict still reads the declared map (separate cache key `served:NAME`, and an object name carries no colon), so an added field is not charged to the object's location. No false refusal found.

**`18.object-extension-validation-rule-artifacts-judged.ts` (#33217): holds.** `ObjectExtensionSchema.validations` is `z.array(ValidationRuleSchema)`, and the registry merges it onto the target by name (`mergeValidationsByName`), so the premise "every save of the target runs them" is true on `main`. The locator sentence matches the code: `where` is `object 'T' · ENTRYPATH · validation LABEL`, path `ENTRYPATH.validations.RULE.regex` or `.schema`, and `ENTRYPATH` is the fold's `path` (`packages[J].manifest.` prefixed in an artifact, `objectExtensions[0]` at the door). The name-keyed `validations.RULE` spelling differs from the #33154 expression path (`validations[0]`), but it is the spelling the object's own rules get from this pair of rules, which is what the card asks for.

**`validate-expressions.ts`: agrees.** The two changed reads and the three comment rewrites say what the code does. The lazily filled index is safe to share: both readings are pure functions of the stack.

**`validate-rule-compilability.ts` / `validate-rule-schema-formats.ts`: agree.** One walk, both rules, so they cannot disagree about which rules exist; `conditional` branches flatten through the same `flattenRules`; one entry per package per target, as the registry keeps them.

**`authoring-rules.ts`: agrees.** Both rules cross together (#7220 family discipline), and the differential claim in the comment is what `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet` builds.

Findings:

- **F1 · nit** — changeset prose. "Unchanged: ... an object's own rules, formulas and hops, at the same locations" overstates: an object's own formula or rule hopping through a lookup an extension adds is newly refused at the build, at the object's location (the PR pins exactly that as a LIT case). The semantic entry's surface covers the shape, so the contract is right; only the changeset sentence is loose. Fix on the prose face or leave.
- **F2 · nit** — tie sentence at the door. "A lookup two packages add at the same priority is not judged" holds at the build. At the `object_extension` door the sibling package's same-named field arrives already folded into the live object, the snapshot carries one extension, and no tie is seen: the written entry's definition is judged. Refusing direction, needs two packages adding one field name to one object at one priority, and the same door reading #33205 already ships for field types. Read, not probed. Accepted deviation; a follow-up card only if a tenant meets it.
- **F3 · nit** — cost at the extension door. Every `object_extension` publish (Studio add-field included) now runs both artifact rules over the closure's live objects in both passes, so a tenant with `json_schema` rules on those objects loads ajv and compiles them twice per extension publish even when the entry carries no rule. Same bill the object door already pays; the comment's "only when the judged snapshot carries a `json_schema` validation" stays true. Noted, no change asked.
- **F4 · nit** — a rule an extension adds that a later layer replaces by name (and so never runs) is still judged. Parity with the #33154 walk and with an object's own shadowed rule; no change asked.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-0m40gx`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**

No governed path, under 3000 lines: Tier S, seat lands.
- **前提实测:** seat read the diff: a stack with no `objectExtensions` is untouched (`objectsAsServed` returns the declared array); the `object` door and every other door are unchanged; #33246's region of `validate-expressions.ts` is not touched (serial fence held).
- **门禁 check-runs:** on this head 68 runs: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. Narrowing arm: dev's dogfood battery green (464 files / 3927 tests, report 6882304973).

- **范围外去向:** none. #33246 (p2) is dispatched after this merges (same file region).
- **落地条款:** ready + auto-merge now under the maintainer's standing order 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z). K = 6 commits on `main` past the run's affected-set base `b63c8949`, below 15: no merge of main owed.
